request.initial_prompt: What is understood by a republican government in the United States is the slow and quiet action of society upon itself. It is a regular state of things really founded upon the enlightened will of the people. It is a conciliatory government under which resolutions are allowed time to ripen; and in which they are deliberately discussed, and executed with mature judgment. The republicans in the United States set a high value upon morality, respect religious belief, and acknowledge the existence of rights. They profess to think that a people ought to be moral, religious, and temperate, in proportion as it is free. What is called the republic in the United States, is the tranquil rule of the majority, which, after having had time to examine itself, and to give proof of its existence, is the common source of all the powers of the State. But the power of the majority is not of itself unlimited. In the moral world humanity, justice, and reason enjoy an undisputed supremacy; in the political world vested rights are treated with no less deference.

common source of all the powers of the State. But the power of the majority is not of itself

unlimited. In the moral world humanity, justice, and reason enjoy an undisputed supremacy. In the political world vested rights are treated with no less deference. The majority recognizes these two barriers, and if it now and then overstep them, it is because, like individuals, it has passions, and like them, it is prone to do what is wrong, whilst it discerns what is right.
